references.text: Parallel action: Humble bowing as an expression of reverence in Abraham's house (toward humans versus toward God).
Theological parallel: Abraham's consistent attitude of humble bowing both before God and before people.
Parallel action: Humble bowing by two great leaders, but with different objects (God versus humans).
Parallel action: Humble bowing by Abraham and his servant (toward humans versus toward God).
Narrative connection: The purchase of the tomb (with bowing) ensures that Abraham can be united with his people (Gen 25:8).
Contrast: Voluntary humble bowing (Abraham) versus forced submission under a yoke (Jeremiah).
Contrast/parallel: Humble bowing by Abraham (toward humans) versus the people (toward God).
